findings.text: the claim_attempt_entry docstring states that an entry omitting claim_token or claim_seq 'is compared against a null and writes nothing at all', but the append's WHERE clause at graph_foundation.py:936 opens with `entry.claim_token IS NULL OR ...`, so omitting the token does not fail closed — it removes the fence and the receipt is written unconditionally. Only a missing claim_seq fails closed. A future claim-ending writer that follows this docstring and passes no token would write an unfenced receipt onto a claim it no longer holds, which is the exact stale-duplicate the fence exists to stop. Omitting the token is legitimate for the sweep (orphan_sweep.py:203 says so explicitly), so the defect is the docstring promising a refusal the statement does not give.

_stored_outcome_claim_entries reads run_id and batch_key from the caller's item, and the only production producer of the rows this writer consumes, worker_common.py::_claimed_source_outcome, sets neither key (it builds sns_id, source_id, claim_token, claim_seq, status, last_error, skip_reason, skip_reason_detail only). Every refused, skipped and requeued receipt therefore stores run_id=null and batch_key=null — the outcomes a failure census most needs to attribute to a run and a batch. The manifest's landing line nonetheless states 'every entry carries claim_seq, source_id and run_id', which is false on this path; per-source attribution still works through source_id and claim_seq, so the census is not blocked.

changed_paths omits imas_codex/standard_names/graph_store/graph_foundation.py, which carries the whole receipt writer (186 added lines: the outcome enum, the entry builder, the append Cypher, append_claim_attempts and record_claim_attempts), and lists imas_codex/standard_names/graph_store/graph_cost_and_claims.py, which the diff does not touch at all (git diff --stat over the reviewed range returns nothing for it). The grant was widened to cover graph_foundation.py and the three test files, and crew check --manifest now reports ok:true, so the fence is satisfied — but a coordinator reading changed_paths to audit the diff would look for the core of the change in the wrong file and find nothing where the writer lives.

section A of the recorded negative-control run reports '12 failed, 10 passed, 1 deselected' over 23 tests and names failing ids that do not exist at the reviewed head — test_produced_writer_stores_a_produced_receipt and test_released_writer_stores_a_released_receipt_with_its_reason were replaced in this round by test_persist_claimed_attachments_stores_a_produced_receipt and test_the_binding_lock_stores_a_released_receipt_with_its_collision; the head test file collects 26 items. So the claim_seq mutation arm was not re-run against the delivered test file, and the fragment's '12 tests fail' figure describes the previous round's file. Sections B, C and the released/stored/produced mutations do name head tests and are current.

in the new transaction block of persist_claimed_source_outcomes the Cypher literal and its 'batch=batch,' argument sit at column 12 inside a call opened at column 16, and 'tx.commit()' is indented to column 16 while the call it terminates began at column 16 inside the same try — the block parses and behaves correctly, but the misleading indentation makes the statement look as though it escapes the try, and the same shape recurs at graph_source_bindings.py:1557, 1684 and 1793. A reader auditing that the receipt and the status write commit as a pair has to count spaces to see it.

the append writes a second per-source append-only audit event family (StandardNameSourceClaimAttempt + HAS_CLAIM_ATTEMPT) beside the existing StandardNameSourceRetry + HAS_RETRY_EVENT owner at graph_source_bindings.py:2351, which already records why a source was parked and is written from four places (attachment_audit.py:483 and :652, graph_source_bindings.py:2442 and :2588, provenance_lifecycle.py:1331). The new type is not a textual copy and carries outcomes the retry event cannot express (produced, released, requeued, batch_failed), so it is an adjacent capability rather than a fork; but the repository now owns two event trails on the same node with overlapping audit intent, and nothing in the fragment says which one a future census should prefer.
